concepts.title: Of Questions and Statements
concepts.definition: Data work begins with a question: a statement like the class drinks more milk than water is a claim, and answering it needs data, collected values that can be organised, shown and judged against the statement.
concepts.key_idea: Data answers questions: every good claim asks for numbers, and every collected number needs a fair question.
question_patterns: turn the given statement into a data question
what data would you collect to check a claim about your class
why is a question needed before collecting data
decide whether the given statement can be checked by data
plan a small survey for one question of your own
how do statements differ from questions in data work

concepts.title: Finding the Mean
concepts.definition: The mean shares the total equally among all values: add the values to get the total and divide by how many there are, giving the balanced centre of the data.
concepts.key_idea: The mean is fair sharing: the total poured equally into every value leaves everyone at the same level.
question_patterns: find the mean of 2 4 and 6
the total of 5 scores is 450 find the mean
find the mean of 12 15 9 and 20
why is the mean called a measure of the centre
the mean height of 4 friends is 140 cm find their total height
check the mean by sharing the total equally

solution_steps.explain: The total is the sum of every value in the data.
Sharing the total among all values gives the mean.

concepts.title: The Median: Middle of Ordered Data
concepts.definition: The median sits at the middle of data arranged in order: with an odd count it is the middle value, with an even count it is the mean of the two middle values, and it is unmoved by extreme values.
concepts.key_idea: Order first, then find the middle: the median reports where the data really leans, ignoring loud extremes.
question_patterns: find the median of 7 3 9 5 and 11
find the median of 4 8 6 10 and 2
why must data be ordered before finding the median
find the median of an even number of values
compare the mean and median of the given data
which is a fairer centre when one value is very large

concepts.title: Extremes and Variability
concepts.definition: Two data sets can share a mean yet differ wildly: their minimum, maximum and spread describe variability, and looking at extremes reveals what averages quietly hide.
concepts.key_idea: The centre is not the whole story: two identical means can hide two very different moods of data.
